metadata.title: 2048-pygame
metadata.description: Single-player 2048 with theme and target selection, a timed new-game introduction, directional merging, random tile spawning, restart confirmation, and result-screen replay.

variables.name: Menu 0, introduction 1, play 2, result 3, restart confirmation 4

events.name: Place tile or retry occupied location

actions.name: Play with selected theme and difficulty
Ask to restart the current game
Confirm restart, retaining theme and difficulty
Play another round with the same selections

systems.name: Spawn the first two tiles after one second
Sample uniformly from board coordinates with rejection of occupied cells
Second starting tile is also two
Spawn an equally likely two or four after a changed move
Show win result after completed spawn
Show loss when full and no neighboring tiles merge

goals.name: Merge a tile equal to the menu-selected target

invariants.name: Difficulty is unselected or a menu target
Theme is unselected, light or dark

assumptions: The source's one-second blocking introduction is represented as 60 logical ticks at 60 Hz; movement is gated until it completes.
Results are nonterminal to permit the source's Y replay to reset only the round while preserving theme and target. Source Q and applicable N controls are host quit commands, not Rule actions.
The unchanged-move test uses a nearly full board whose sole post-merge vacancy must receive the random tile; either possible tile value leaves the repeated left move unchanged.

unresolved.reason: The source clears the theme selection and difficulty highlight on a click outside every menu button. The accepted Scene has no selectable background target and this backend cancels UI-background clicks. An unfiltered click binding would also clear selections on an ineligible Play click.

Gameplay moves on a primary-button drag of at least 24 source pixels in its dominant direction. This backend emits confirmed clicks, not pointer displacement or drag gestures, so it cannot route the four source swipe directions.

The source handles Q in menu and gameplay but ignores it in blocking restart and result prompts; N quits only in those prompts. Input contexts cannot activate by Rule stage, and host quit has no Rule precondition. The Q and N quit bindings above therefore cannot preserve these stage restrictions exactly.
